$comment: The certificate the production PostgreSQL primary is expected to serve.
scripts/check-primary-tls.ts probes the live endpoint against this and runs nightly
from .github/workflows/railway-drift.yml, so the certificate is declared state rather
than something a deploy can quietly change.
`pendingRollout` is how the check tells the truth before the rollout has happened:
the certificate served today IS on the rejected list, so the run warns loudly until
warnUntil and fails hard after it. Clear both it and `expected` together when the
private CA is minted -- see docs/pg-primary-tls-rollout.md.

rejectedFingerprints.D9:F6:91:05:8E:A7:95:D3:23:FC:33:5F:E4:2: The Debian snakeoil certificate from postgres:18.6-bookworm. Its private key is published in that public image layer, so anyone can impersonate the primary to a client that does not verify. If the primary serves this again, a deploy has reverted the TLS material.

pendingRollout.reason: The private CA has not been minted and the primary still serves the base image certificate. Tracked in docs/pg-primary-tls-rollout.md.
